candidatePledges.paraphrase: Enable Medicare to negotiate prescription prices with reach intended beyond Medicare beneficiaries to public and private purchasers.
candidatePledges.locator: Bringing Down Drug Prices and Taking on the Pharmaceutical Industry; paragraph beginning 'Too many Americans struggle'
candidatePledges.criterion: Code Medicare legal negotiating authority separately from scope for all public/private purchasers, drug coverage, prices paid, and effective date.
candidatePledges.uncertainty: IRA authorizes selected Medicare drug negotiations; it does not by itself establish all-purchaser negotiating authority. First negotiated prices scheduled to apply in 2026 after 2021-25 administration; distinguish enactment from price availability.

candidatePledges.paraphrase: Cap seniors' out-of-pocket prescription drug costs.
candidatePledges.locator: Bringing Down Drug Prices and Taking on the Pharmaceutical Industry; same paragraph, sentence on senior out-of-pocket costs
candidatePledges.criterion: Evaluate scope of capped Medicare Part D covered prescriptions separately from all seniors, uncovered medicines and beneficiary realized spending.
candidatePledges.uncertainty: Medicare Part D $2,000 annual threshold began January 2025; not equivalent to cap on every prescription expense for all seniors; no independent coding.

candidatePledges.paraphrase: End the UK non-domicile tax status/remittance basis and replace it with a limited residence-based foreign-income regime.
candidatePledges.locator: Strong foundations; Labour will address unfairness in the tax system; non-dom paragraph
candidatePledges.criterion: Separate statutory abolition of remittance basis, effective date, replacement four-year foreign income and gains relief, and trust/legacy transition rules.
candidatePledges.uncertainty: Conservative Spring Budget 2024 proposed abolishing the remittance basis before Labour won; cross-party policy continuity is a competing explanation. The Labour manifesto also promised changes to offshore trusts, requiring separate atomization.

officialEvents.locator: First 10 Part D drugs selected for 2026 price applicability
officialEvents.fact: CMS selected ten Part D drugs for the initial negotiation cycle; selection is not negotiated price in effect.

officialEvents.locator: First ten drug price agreements and January 1 2026 applicability
officialEvents.fact: CMS announced negotiated prices for ten selected drugs, scheduled for Jan 1 2026; reported hypothetical savings are modeled, not observed fiscal outlays.

officialEvents.locator: Part D out-of-pocket annual cap went into effect January 1 2025
officialEvents.fact: CMS confirms $2,000 Part D annual out-of-pocket cap effective Jan 1 2025; 2026 indexed threshold $2,100.
Qualified FLSA overtime premium deduction, capped $12,500/$25,000 with income phaseout, tax years 2025-28; not all overtime pay and not a payroll-tax exemption.
Ended availability of remittance basis for tax year 2025-26 onward, subject to transitional rules.

officialEvents.locator: Removal of remittance basis 6 April 2025; four-year FIG exceptions
officialEvents.fact: HMRC guidance confirms new residence-based rules and qualified four-year relief, with prior-year remittance treatment preserved.

officialEvents.locator: BGBl 2025 I Nr 361, Gesetz vom 22 Dezember 2025; EStG §3 Nr 21
officialEvents.fact: Law promulgated Dec 23 2025, effective Jan 1 2026, exempts up to EUR 24,000/year qualifying post-retirement-age employee wages; excludes self-employed and civil servants.
BMF confirms up to EUR 2,000 per month qualifying wages tax exempt from Jan 1 2026; social insurance contributions continue.

officialEvents.locator: Council of Ministers proposal: 19% 2026, 18% 2027, 17% 2028, SME 15% first EUR 50k
officialEvents.fact: Government approved a proposed staged corporate tax cut; announcement is not enacted law, revenue or corporate effective tax paid.

officialEvents.locator: Lei 55-A/2025, article 2; IRS Code article 68, effective 2025-07-23
officialEvents.fact: Changed national progressive IRS statutory rates in 2025; no independently verified EUR 500 million realized revenue effect.

officialEvents.locator: Lei 64/2025, article 2 IRC Code article 87 and article 3 transitional rates
officialEvents.fact: Enacted 17% general corporate tax rate for tax periods from 2028, transitional 19% for 2026 and 18% for 2027; SME rate changes apply from 2026. Enacted rates are not actual effective tax paid.
Parliament authorized government to reduce first six IRS brackets within 180 days; authorization alone does not establish effective rate changes.

officialEvents.locator: 29 October 2026 cabinet announcement, first six income tax brackets
officialEvents.fact: Cabinet announced approval of a decree-law with retroactive intended effect to January 2026; final promulgation/publication not independently verified.
